files.purpose: New in B3 (commit d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups ... shared MCP and provider code'): a non-final @MainActor base class that owns the one floating NSPanel, the Escape key monitor and the present/close lifecycle that MCPKeyPanel (width 380) and MCPSetupPanel (width 400) previously each duplicated verbatim in B2. present(_:) measures the SwiftUI content at the fixed width, sizes the panel to max(height, 100), parks it 24 points in from the top-right of NSScreen.main's visibleFrame, installs the Escape monitor and orders it front without activating the app; close() removes the monitor and orders the panel out. It is lifted text-for-text from the B2 bodies with the literal 380/400 replaced by the stored width, so neither panel's observable behaviour changes.
key_symbols: @MainActor class FloatingGuidePanel (non-final; subclassed by final class MCPKeyPanel and final class MCPSetupPanel)
private(set) var panel: NSPanel? (:8, readable by subclasses: MCPSetupPanel.isPresenting and fit(height:) use it)
func close() (:28-31, overridable; MCPSetupPanel overrides it to clear presentedEntryID then call super.close())
calls_into: NSScreen.main?.visibleFrame and NSPanel.setFrameOrigin(NSPoint(x: visible.maxX - width - 24, y: visible.maxY - panel.frame.height - 24)) (:21-23)
NSPanel(contentRect: width x 200, styleMask: [.nonactivatingPanel, .fullSizeContentView, .titled, .closable], backing: .buffered, defer: false) (:34-39)
self.close() from the monitor, dynamically dispatched so MCPSetupPanel's override runs (:62)
state_owned: panel: NSPanel? - created lazily once per instance by makePanel() and reused on every later present (:18, :54)
escapeMonitor: Any? - non-nil exactly while a monitor is installed; startEscapeMonitor guards on nil so it is installed at most once (:59)
width: CGFloat - fixed at init (380 for MCPKeyPanel.shared, 400 for MCPSetupPanel.shared)
side_effects: creates one floating NSPanel per subclass singleton on first present
installs an app-local key-down NSEvent monitor on present and removes it on close
Escape (keyCode 53) while the panel is visible is swallowed (monitor returns nil) and closes the panel; any other key, or any key while the panel is hidden, passes through
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSPanel with .nonactivatingPanel: shown with orderFrontRegardless and never activates the app (Windows: ED-063 WS_EX_NOACTIVATE plus a thread-local WH_CBT hook, see PR-MCP-215)
panel.level = .floating (always above normal windows), collectionBehavior [.canJoinAllSpaces, .fullScreenAuxiliary], hidesOnDeactivate = false
NSScreen.main visibleFrame in bottom-left-origin coordinates: origin y = visible.maxY - panel height - 24 puts the top edge 24 points below the visible top
window shadow via hasShadow = true on a non-opaque, clear-background window
ui_elements: The shared floating guide panel container: fixed width (380 key panel / 400 setup panel), height = content fitting height rounded up with a floor of 100, initial contentRect height 200, hidden title, transparent title bar, movable by background, floating level, all spaces, full-screen auxiliary, clear non-opaque background with shadow, all three traffic-light buttons hidden (comment :49-50: the panel closes from its own xmark and on Escape), placed 24 points in from the top-right of the main screen's visible frame
feature_notes: Status A: the file does not exist at B2. Its entire body (present sizing/placement/orderFront :17-25, close :28-31, makePanel :33-56, startEscapeMonitor :58-65, stopEscapeMonitor :67-70) is the code B2 duplicated in MCPKeyPanel.swift (B2 :22-30, :33-36, :38-61, :63-75) and MCPSetupPanel.swift (B2 :34-43, :45-49, :63-86, :88-100); the B3 diffs of those two files delete exactly that code and replace it with 'final class X: FloatingGuidePanel', 'private init() { super.init(width: 380|400) }' and 'present(content)'.

The only textual differences from the B2 bodies are the literal 380/400 becoming the stored width, 'private var panel' becoming 'private(set) var panel' on the base, and MCPSetupPanel's close becoming 'override func close() { presentedEntryID = nil; super.close() }'. The override reorders the B2 sequence (stopEscapeMonitor, presentedEntryID = nil, orderOut) to (presentedEntryID = nil, stopEscapeMonitor, orderOut); all three are synchronous main-actor steps, so nothing observable changes.
Escape in the setup panel still clears presentedEntryID: the monitor calls self.close(), which dispatches to MCPSetupPanel's override because FloatingGuidePanel is a non-final class.
Each subclass singleton still owns its own NSPanel and its own escape monitor, so the key panel and the setup panel remain two separate windows, exactly as in B2.

No spec record cites FloatingGuidePanel.swift yet. PR-MCP-214, PR-MCP-215, PR-MCP-216, PR-MCP-220, UI-MCP-070 and UI-MCP-078 cite the B2 MCPKeyPanel/MCPSetupPanel line ranges whose code now lives here; their behaviour text remains correct and only their source_evidence (plus the ':41' / ':66 .nonactivatingPanel' pointers in the PR-MCP-215 windows_path and the UI-MCP-070/078 notes, now FloatingGuidePanel.swift:36) needs re-citing.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED (port, not source): the C# ports of the two panels, which the B3 source now makes one shared implementation, do not match each other. src/Marrow.App/Views/Settings/MCPKeyPanel.cs sets ShowActivated=false, keeps Topmost=true, uses TransparencyLevelHint Transparent, installs the ED-063 WH_CBT activation hook and adds/removes the Escape handler per present/close. src/Marrow.App/Views/Settings/MCPSetupPanel.cs has no ShowActivated=false and no WH_CBT hook, sets Topmost=true then Topmost=false after Show (so it does not stay at the floating level), uses AcrylicBlur, attaches the Escape handler permanently in MakePanel without the isVisible check, and places with Math.Ceiling/RenderScaling where the key panel uses Math.Round/screen.Scaling. A grep of porting/platform_adaptations.md and porting/unknowns.md for MCPSetupPanel found no recorded deviation covering these. Whether any of them is an intended, recorded deviation needs checking before the shared C# base is extracted.
